---
title: "07 · Estimation vs prediction"
subtitle: "A model that explains an average relationship is not automatically good at predicting a new patient."
---

::: {.topic-banner}
**The clinical question**

Are we estimating how an exposure relates to an outcome, or predicting what will happen for a new patient?
:::

::: {.learning-outcomes}
### By the end of this topic

- Distinguish explanatory and predictive modelling goals.
- Explain training performance, generalisation, and overfitting.
- Describe the purpose of train/test splits and external validation.
- Recognise when calibration and discrimination matter for clinical risk scores.
:::

## Core ideas

Estimation focuses on a parameter and its uncertainty. Prediction focuses on performance for unseen observations. Adding complexity can improve fit to the development data while harming generalisation. Validation should mimic the intended clinical use.

::: {.clinical-lens}
**Ask:** Who will receive this prediction, at what point in care, what action follows, and was performance assessed in a sufficiently similar population?
:::
